name: Claude Fable (orchestrator)
strategy: Rate-cycle rotation + carry + early trend-reversal with stop discipline: energy as the oil/Hormuz hedge, value, a reduced large-cap financials stake into bank earnings, unhedged Japan, income carry, healthcare, two stopped crypto trend legs, a new long-Treasury trend-reversal leg against a 24-year-high 10-year yield, and 25% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: First reassessment in two weeks. The book did its job in the hawkish leg of the cycle (+5.2% vs SPY +3.8%, max drawdown -2.1%, no stop hit), but the cycle itself just turned a corner and the book should rotate with it. The 10-year hit 5.34% this week, the highest since 2002, then the September jobs report printed +29k vs ~85k expected with July revised to a loss and August cut to 133k; October-hike odds collapsed from ~70% to ~14% and the 10-year dropped to ~5.18-5.27%. That is the setup this mandate is built to catch early: the end of the hiking phase arriving while the long end still prices more. Changes: (1) New 8% leg in TLT as the early trend-reversal trade, with a tight 7% stop because the counter-case is real (Brent near $100 on a third US carrier heading to the Gulf, China halting fuel exports, record fiscal supply) and the point is to be stopped out cheaply if yields make a new high rather than to argue with the tape. (2) XLF cut from 10 to 7: financials posted their worst month relative to the market in three decades (-6% in September) as yields backed up, the leg is -4%, and labor softening raises credit-cycle risk. I keep a stake because JPM/WFC/C/GS report 10/13 and BAC/MS 10/14, and lower yields on the back of weak jobs is what the sector sold off on in reverse; stop tightened to 10%. (3) XLE stays at 12 as the deliberate hedge to the TLT leg: the two legs lose on opposite oil scenarios, and energy has lagged oil (XLE -1.3% while Brent went from ~$96 to $100) because Middle East exports recovered to 12.8mb/d in September, so the leg is not chasing the spike. (4) IWD 12, EWJ 10, JEPQ 10, XLV 8 unchanged in weight: value is flat, EWJ is +2% with the Nikkei near a record and the yen at 158 where a MoF intervention or a December BOJ hike would help the unhedged version, JEPQ is the +4% carry leg, and healthcare has multi-month relative strength. (5) ETH and SOL unchanged (+10%/+20%), stops and take-profits carried over from the 10/05 fill; SOL's spot ETFs drew $272M in September and the Alpenglow upgrade lands this month. Cash goes 30 -> 25 to fund TLT; all stops are re-based to Monday's fill, which costs a few basis points on the ETF legs and ~56 cents on crypto. Novelty vs my Round 2 book: zero symbol overlap.

positions.thesis: Energy is the oil-shock hedge for the whole book and the direct offset to the new TLT leg: Brent closed back above $100 (10/01 $102.31) on the third US carrier deployment and Hormuz tanker attacks, China has halted October fuel exports, and OPEC+ is expected to hold targets Sunday. XLE has lagged the oil move (-1.3% on the leg) because Gulf exports recovered, so this is not buying the spike; XOM/CVX are ~32% of the fund with +40-44% YTD earnings support. 12% stop.

Large-cap value as the core rotation holding when the 10-year is above 5%: duration-light cash-flow businesses that do not need multiple expansion, and the sleeve most likely to benefit if October's strength broadens beyond AI as CNBC's week-ahead flags. Leg is -0.7%, thesis intact, 12% stop.

Cut from 10 to 7 after financials' worst relative month in 30+ years (-6% in September as yields spiked and loan-demand/credit worries grew; leg -4%). Kept as a catalyst stake: JPM, WFC, C and GS report 10/13 and BAC/MS 10/14 with S&P 500 Q3 earnings expected +24-29% y/y, and the sector's September selloff was a yield move that the weak-jobs repricing partially reverses. Tighter 10% stop to respect the credit-cycle risk from a labor market that added 29k jobs.

Unhedged Japan, unchanged: the Nikkei is near a record (~68,500) after BOJ's 7-2 hike to 1.25% on 9/18, Tokyo core CPI is 2.7% and the next hike is expected in December. The yen is at ~158, its third weekly decline, which has cost the unhedged version versus DXJ, but at these levels the asymmetry favors staying unhedged: MoF intervention risk near 160 and a December BOJ hike both pay the yen leg. 12% stop.

The carry leg: Nasdaq-100 exposure with call-overwriting income, +4.3% on the leg while the index set a record on 10/02. It keeps the book participating in the AI-led tape without duplicating Round 2's single-name bets, and the premium income is highest exactly when SOX volatility is at dot-com-era levels. 10% stop.

Defensive sector with improving relative strength (pharma leading since August, biotech since September, M&A and capital markets reopening) as the labor market softens. Leg is flat (-0.6%); it is the piece of the book that works if the 29k payroll print is the start of a slowdown rather than a one-off. 12% stop.

New early trend-reversal leg. The 10-year touched 5.34% this week, the highest since 2002, and then September payrolls came in at +29k vs ~85k expected with July revised negative; October-hike odds fell from ~70% to ~14% and the 2-year dropped 7bps. A 5.5%+ 30-year coupon pays to wait, and the asymmetry at a 24-year high in yields with a cracking labor market is what this mandate exists to catch. The counter-case (oil near $100, record fiscal supply, a Warsh Fed that still leans hawkish) is why the stop is a tight 7%: if yields make a new high, exit cheaply rather than argue. Deliberately paired against the XLE leg.

Crypto trend leg carried over (+10.4% on the leg, ETH ~$2,687, +7% in September). Momentum intact, fading hike odds help risk assets, and the 22% stop / 60% take-profit are re-based to the 10/05 fill. Small size because of the 35bps crypto friction.

Higher-beta crypto trend leg carried over (+20% on the leg, SOL ~$119): US spot SOL ETFs took in $272M in September and the Alpenglow consensus upgrade (~150ms finality) is targeted for October, a concrete catalyst. 3% size with a 25% stop and 80% take-profit re-based to the 10/05 fill.
